# package schedule

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-ieee20305/schedule"
```

Package schedule implements IEEE 2030.5 event scheduling: primacy-based control priority, overlapping event resolution, randomization of start and duration, and the active/superseded/cancelled state machine.

A Scheduler holds the events of one function set (DER controls, DRLC controls, tariff intervals, text messages, ...), which FromEvent makes from the generated resources. When events that conflict overlap in time, the scheduler resolves them by primacy (lower values win), then by event creation time (newer wins): the loser is Superseded, and an active loser runs until the winner starts. What conflicts depends on the function set: DERConflicts compares the opMod controls of DERControls, DRLCConflicts the device categories of EndDeviceControls, and otherwise every event conflicts.

A client applies the randomization bounds of the events (Options.Randomize) with offsets drawn deterministically from a seed, and answers the transitions it subscribes to as ResponseRequired says. A server runs the same Scheduler without randomization to keep the EventStatus of its events.

## Functions

### func AllConflict

```go
func AllConflict(a, b Event) bool
```

AllConflict is the Conflicts of a Scheduler without one: every pair of events conflicts, as for pricing, messaging, prepayment and flow reservation.

### func DERConflicts

```go
func DERConflicts(a, b Event) bool
```

DERConflicts reports whether two DERControl events conflict: they set at least one opMod\* control of DERControlBase in common, including those a profile adds (such as the limits of CSIP-AUS). An event whose Value is not a DERControl conflicts with everything.

### func DRLCConflicts

```go
func DRLCConflicts(a, b Event) bool
```

DRLCConflicts reports whether two EndDeviceControl events conflict: their deviceCategory bits intersect. An event whose Value is not an EndDeviceControl conflicts with everything.

### func Precedes

```go
func Precedes(a, b Event) bool
```

Precedes reports whether a takes precedence over b: it has a lower primacy value, or the same primacy and a later creation time, or the same primacy and creation time and a lower MRID, so that the order is total.

### func ResponseRequired

```go
func ResponseRequired(flags []byte, t Transition) (respond bool, responseStatus uint8)
```

ResponseRequired reports whether the transition t calls for a Response, given the responseRequired flags of the event (a HexBinary8; absent is none), and the Response status to send:

  - with RespondReceived, the receipt of an event is ResponseReceived;
  - with RespondReceived or RespondSpecific, the receipt of an event that has already ended is ResponseRejectedExpired;
  - with RespondSpecific, becoming Active is ResponseStarted, Completed ResponseCompleted, Cancelled or CancelledRandom ResponseCancelled, and Superseded ResponseSuperseded.

The responses of the end user are not transitions; send them when the user answers.

## Types

### type Clock

```go
type Clock interface {
	// Now returns the current time.
	Now() time.Time
	// AfterFunc calls f in its own goroutine once d has elapsed, unless
	// the returned Stopper is stopped first. The Scheduler only asks for
	// d > 0 and calls AfterFunc and Stop with its own lock held, so a
	// clock must not call f from within them; a test clock may call f
	// from the goroutine that advances it.
	AfterFunc(d time.Duration, f func()) Stopper
}
```

Clock is the time source of a Scheduler. Tests replace SystemClock with a clock they advance themselves.

```go
var SystemClock Clock = systemClock{}
```

SystemClock is the Clock of the operating system: time.Now and time.AfterFunc.

}

Event is an event of any IEEE 2030.5 Event function set, as the Scheduler sees it. FromEvent makes one from a resource.

#### func FromEvent

```go
func FromEvent(v any, primacy uint8, program string) (Event, error)
```

FromEvent returns the Event of the resource v, a DERControl, EndDeviceControl, TextMessage, TimeTariffInterval, SupplyInterruptionOverride or FlowReservationResponse, or a pointer to one, of a program with the given primacy. The Value of the Event is v.

A SupplyInterruptionOverride is not an Event in IEEE 2030.5: it has no mRID, creation time or status, so its MRID is its href, or else its interval, and it is Scheduled.

The error matches ieee20305.ErrInvalid for a type FromEvent does not know, a nil pointer, an event without mRID, or an unknown currentStatus.

#### func (Event) End

```go
func (e Event) End() time.Time
```

End returns the end of the interval of e, before randomization.

### type Options

```go
type Options struct {
	// Clock is the time source; SystemClock when nil.
	Clock Clock
	// Seed seeds the randomization. Each event draws its random
	// offsets from Seed and its MRID, so they do not depend on the
	// order in which events arrive. Schedulers with the same Seed draw
	// the same offsets for an event: give each device its own, such as
	// its SFDI (as agent.Config does when its Seed is zero).
	Seed uint64
	// Randomize applies the randomizeStart and randomizeDuration of the
	// events, as a client does. A server leaves it off.
	Randomize bool
	// Conflicts reports whether two events compete for the same thing,
	// so that one can supersede the other. When nil, all events
	// conflict. See DERConflicts and DRLCConflicts.
	Conflicts func(a, b Event) bool
}
```

Options configure a Scheduler.

### type Scheduler

```go
type Scheduler struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Scheduler tracks the events of one function set and resolves them into what is active when.

Events that overlap in time and conflict are resolved by precedence (see Precedes): an event that would overlap one of higher precedence is Superseded. An active event that a new event of higher precedence overlaps stays active until that event starts, and is then Superseded. Supersession is final: an event does not come back when the event that superseded it is cancelled or removed. Overlap is judged on the randomized intervals.

The Scheduler moves events through their states on its Clock and reports each change to its subscribers. It is safe for concurrent use.

#### func New

```go
func New(o Options) *Scheduler
```

New returns a Scheduler with options o.

#### func (Scheduler) Active

```go
func (s *Scheduler) Active(at time.Time) []Event
```

Active returns the events planned to be active at at, in order of precedence, with their current state. For a time in the future, this is the plan from the events known now.

#### func (Scheduler) Cancel

```go
func (s *Scheduler) Cancel(mrid string, randomized bool)
```

Cancel cancels the event mrid, as the server does with the status Cancelled, or CancelledRandom when randomized is true. With Randomize on, an active event cancelled with randomization stays active for a random delay within the larger magnitude of its randomizeStart and randomizeDuration, but not past its end. Cancel does nothing to an unknown event or one in a terminal state.

#### func (Scheduler) Close

```go
func (s *Scheduler) Close()
```

Close stops the Scheduler: it ends every subscription, dropping the transitions not yet read, and waits for their goroutines to finish. Afterwards Upsert, Cancel and Remove do nothing.

#### func (Scheduler) Events

```go
func (s *Scheduler) Events() []Event
```

Events returns every event the Scheduler knows, in order of precedence.

#### func (Scheduler) Get

```go
func (s *Scheduler) Get(mrid string) (Event, bool)
```

Get returns the event mrid in its current state.

#### func (Scheduler) Remove

```go
func (s *Scheduler) Remove(mrid string) bool
```

Remove forgets the event mrid without a transition, and reports whether there was one. The events it superseded stay superseded.

#### func (Scheduler) Subscribe

```go
func (s *Scheduler) Subscribe() (<-chan Transition, func())
```

Subscribe returns a channel of every transition from now on, in order, and a function that ends the subscription and closes the channel. The Scheduler never waits for a subscriber: transitions queue until it reads them. Close ends every subscription.

#### func (Scheduler) Timeline

```go
func (s *Scheduler) Timeline(from, to time.Time) []Segment
```

Timeline divides \[from, to) into the segments in which the same events are planned to be active, as Active reports them.

#### func (Scheduler) Upsert

```go
func (s *Scheduler) Upsert(e Event)
```

Upsert adds the event e, or updates the event with its MRID.

A new event is reported as received, then resolved against the others. An e with Status Cancelled or CancelledRandom cancels the event as Cancel does, and one with Status Superseded or Completed moves it to that state; Scheduled and Active are ignored, since the Scheduler works out when the event is active itself. An update of an event in a terminal state changes its fields but not its state.

#### func (Scheduler) Window

```go
func (s *Scheduler) Window(mrid string) (start, end time.Time, ok bool)
```

Window returns the span in which the event mrid is planned to be active: its randomized interval, cut short by an event that supersedes it or by a randomized cancellation. ok is false when the event is not planned to be active, because it is unknown or in a terminal state.

### type Status

```go
type Status uint8
```

Status is the state of an event: the currentStatus codes of an IEEE 2030.5 EventStatus. Completed is new in IEEE 2030.5-2023, and servers of earlier revisions do not send it.

```go
const (
	// Scheduled is an event that has not started yet.
	Scheduled Status = 0
	// Active is an event that is in effect.
	Active Status = 1
	// Cancelled is an event the server cancelled.
	Cancelled Status = 2
	// CancelledRandom is an event the server cancelled with
	// randomization: an active event ends after a random delay.
	CancelledRandom Status = 3
	// Superseded is an event that lost to a conflicting, overlapping
	// event of higher precedence. IEEE 2030.5-2023 deprecates it for
	// servers, which leave supersession to the clients.
	Superseded Status = 4
	// Completed is an event whose interval has ended, or that was
	// received after its interval ended.
	Completed Status = 5
)
```

The states of an event.

### type Transition

```go
type Transition struct {
	// Event is the event, with Status To.
	Event    Event
	From, To Status
	// At is the time of the transition by the Clock.
	At time.Time
}
```

Transition is a change of state of an event. The receipt of a new event is a Transition with From equal to To: its initial state, which is Scheduled, Completed for an event received after it ended, or the cancelled or superseded state the event arrived with. Transitions out of the initial state follow it.
